title: Urban Function and Day–Night Surface Thermal Heterogeneity Across the Guangdong–Hong Kong– Macao Greater Bay Area
content: Regional thermal assessment requires interpretable land characteristics and evaluation of model transferability across jurisdictions. We integrated open settlement, building height, land cover, terrain, climate and summer land surface temperature (LST) data for 9093 urban 1 km grid cells in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area. City-adjusted regression, covariate matching and spatially separated validation evaluated the contribution of urban function beyond cover and morphology. Non-residential share was positively associated with daytime LST and negatively associated with nighttime LST; these signs persisted in daily-product and earlier-window checks on 3358 cells. In a balanced subset of 368 matched pairs, non-residential-enriched cells were 0.319 °C warmer by day and 0.189 °C cooler by night. The daytime contrast was sensitive to city weighting, and the observation-qualified subset lacked balanced matches. Morphology provided stronger cross-city predictive gains than function, whose addition reduced boosting root mean squared error by 0.002 °C by day and 0.011 °C by night; gains varied across sensitivity analyses. The framework links thermal differentiation to sample comparability and predictive transferability, supporting geographically targeted assessment with open geospatial data. Temporal mismatch, clear-sky sampling and functional proxies limit causal interpretation.
